title: Understanding Sync and Send
goal: Learn how Send and Sync control thread safety at compile time.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 4 Afternoon: Send and Sync

sections.text: In Rust, thread safety is governed by two marker traits named `Send` and `Sync`. The compiler uses them to prevent data races before your code runs.

sections.caption: Types like String implement Send and can be moved into another thread.

sections.text: `Send` indicates that a value can transfer ownership to another thread. Most Rust types implement `Send` automatically if all their fields implement `Send`.
`Sync` indicates that a value can be shared across threads through an immutable reference. A type `T` is `Sync` if and only if `&T` is `Send`.

sections.caption: Mutex wraps a Send type and makes it Sync by controlling concurrent access.

sections.text: Types like `Rc` implement neither `Send` nor `Sync` because their reference counter is not atomic. Multi-threaded code must use `Arc` and `Mutex` instead.

explanation: Learn how Send and Sync control thread safety at compile time.
